Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTS A PASSENGER TRAIN CAUGHT ON FIRE, RESULTING IN THE EVACUATION OF 200 PASSENGERS. THERE WERE NO REPORTED INJURIES OR FATALITIES. THE SUSPECTED CAUSE OF THE FIRE IS A PANEL HANGING OFF THE TRAIN THAT MADE CONTACT WITH THE THIRD RAIL. AT LEAST 1 CAR IS HEAVILY DAMAGED, BUT AN EXACT DAMAGE ESTIMATE WAS NOT REPORTED. SOME RAIL TIES WERE ALSO ON FIRE. THIS OCCURRED ON THE BRIDGE WITH LIMITED ACCESS AND THE CAR HAD TO BE TRANSFERRED TO A NEARBY YARD FOR FIREFIGHTING PURPOSES. Report Description
DURING AN ASSESSMENT OF THE LAKE WASHINGTON, SOUTHEAST FACILITY, A DRY GAS LEAK WAS OBSERVED FROM AN EL PASO GAS BUY BACK LIKE ASSOCIATED WITH THE SL 10854 #2 WELL. A VALVE ON THE LINE IS SET TO OPEN DURING LOW PRESSURE AT THE FACILITY. SHUT IN CONDITIONS DURING HURRICANE ISAAC CAUSE LOW PRESSURE AT THE FACILITY, CAUSING THE VALVE TO OPEN AND PRESSURE UP THE LINE. A HOLE IN THE LINE, ASSUME TO BE CREATED BY HURRICANE DAMAGE, WAS RELEASING DRY GAS. NO SHEEN WAS OBSERVED AT THE RELEASE. THE LINE IS A 4” OD LINE AND APPROXIMATELY 5000’ LONG. THE LINE HAS BEEN ISOLATED AND OPERATORS ARE OBSERVING THE LINE WHILE IT BLEEDS DOWN TO ATMOSPHERE.

THE MATERIAL WAS RELEASED ONTO THE ASPHALT AND THEN INTO THE STORM WATER SYSTEM WHICH LEADS TO OUTFALL 15. OUTFALL 15 DRAINS TO THE JAMES RIVER AND IT HAS BEEN CONFIRMED SOME DID MAKE IT INTO THE RIVER. A HOLE IN THE BOTTOM OF THE TANKER FROM AN UNKNOWN REASON CAUSED THE RELEASE.
